gifts.title: Where to actually park near Grand Ave without paying
gifts.for_complaint: Paying for street parking is pushing customers to other locations
gifts.deliverable: One-page printable guide (URL + PDF/sign for the front desk and mirror stations) showing free street-parking blocks, nearest free lots, and walk time from 867 Grand Ave, so front desk can hand it to every caller who asks about parking
gifts.inputs_needed: St. Paul public parking/signage rules for the Grand Ave corridor and a public map of nearby lots — both public data, no account needed, fully reachable today
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Two separate reviewers name the exact reason they stopped or reconsidered coming: paid parking. One explicitly switched to a different GENT location over it. This is the one complaint we can fully resolve today with zero cost and zero involvement from them.

gifts.title: A real Grand Ave, St. Paul page — the live site only shows Minneapolis
gifts.for_complaint: Location confusion — gentcg.com resolves to /locations/minneapolis/, and this St. Paul shop isn't on OpenStreetMap either
gifts.deliverable: Standalone HTML page at a URL: correct 867 Grand Ave address, hours, phone, embedded public map, the parking guide above, and top stylists customers actually name in reviews (Ashley, Mo, Mercedes, Kristin, Ari) with how long each has been mentioned
gifts.inputs_needed: Current hours and phone number, pulled from the shop's public Google Business Profile listing — public, reachable, no login
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: Right now the only live page for this business points to the wrong city. A visitor searching 'GENT St Paul' lands nowhere authoritative — this is the single missing asset that fixes it, built from data that's already public.

gifts.title: Print the stylist wall customers already wrote for you
gifts.for_complaint: High stylist turnover / can't keep good employees — loyalty is to the chair, not the shop
gifts.deliverable: A printable one-page sign/PDF for the front desk or mirror stations listing the stylists 500 reviewers actually name by hand (Ashley, Mo, Mercedes, Kristin, Ari, Patrick) with how many reviews mention each and what they're known for (fades, beard/razor work, kids' cuts) — so a new client picks a stylist instead of just picking a chair
gifts.inputs_needed: Nothing beyond the review corpus already supplied
gifts.why_they_stop_and_read: This isn't a generic 'meet the team' page — it's their own customers' words about their own staff, counted and printed. It's the cheapest possible hedge against the exact key-person risk their own reviews describe.
